transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-17 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Dana Kim (Redwood SE), Maya Lopez (CTO - CrestPoint), Jordan Reeves (Head of Infrastructure), Priya Nair (Security Engineer)

Summary: Short intake to understand CrestPoint's security constraints for an LLM fingerprinting/search product. Main topics: SOC2/ISO evidence, SSO/SAML integration, RBAC needs, audit logs and retention, encryption/KMS options (cloud KMS vs customer-managed HSM), data residency, Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs, and next steps for a pilot.

Topics: SOC2/ISO, SSO, RBAC, audit logs, KMS, on-prem/air-gapped options, SLAs, pricing comparison, deployment timeline.

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Samir, AE from Redwood, and with me is Dana, our Solutions Engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Maya: Doing well, thanks. We wanted to get into the nitty-gritty on security and options for deployment — whether Hosted will work or we need Dedicated or Private.
[00:12] Jordan: Yeah, we run highly regulated financial analytics, so encryption, auditability, and SSO are non-negotiable.
[00:17] Dana: Understood. We'll try to map our controls to yours. Quick question up front — do you already have SOC 2 plus ISO requirements, or is it just SOC2 on the roadmap?
[00:25] Priya: Both. SOC 2 Type II is live, and ISO 27001 is in progress. We're collecting artifacts for vendor due diligence.
[00:31] Samir: Great. We can share our SOC 2 Type II report and ISO attestations — that's part of the next steps. Also we have an enterprise security questionnaire we can hand over.
[00:39] Maya: Perfect. On SSO — we use Okta and have SAML 2.0 for our external systems, and we use SCIM for provisioning.
[00:46] Dana: Redwood supports SAML SSO and SCIM-based provisioning for RBAC. For Hosted customers we provide SP-initiated and IdP-initiated SSO; for Private, you control the IdP endpoints.
[00:54] Jordan: Do you support enforcing roles at the token level so engineers can't accidentally call production models? We need strict RBAC across models and environments.
[01:02] Dana: Yes. We expose role mappings and route-level permissions. You can bind roles to specific model endpoints, and audit logs record which token invoked which model.
[01:11] Priya: Speaking of audit logs, what's the retention window and can we export them to our SIEM?
[01:16] Samir: We have configurable retention. By default hosted audit logs are kept 90 days, but enterprise customers can extend retention or push to customer-owned S3 or a logging pipeline. Exports to Splunk/Datadog/Elastic are supported.
[01:26] Priya: We need at least 365 days retention and an immutable export to our AWS account. Also integrity checks and tamper-evidence would be good.
[01:33] Dana: For Dedicated and Private customers we can ship logs to your AWS account or to an on-prem collector. immutable storage patterns and signed log chains are possible as an add-on; we'll detail options in the security pack.
[01:44] Maya: Good. Encryption at rest and in transit? KMS options?
[01:49] Dana: TLS in transit end-to-end. For at-rest we encrypt with cloud KMS by default. For customer-managed keys we support BYOK via cloud KMS and HSM integration — you can bring keys from AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault, or use a customer HSM that we can integrate via KMIP in Private deployments.
[02:03] Jordan: Do you offer HSM-backed signing for model artifacts and weights? We want provenance for models used in production.
[02:09] Samir: We can sign model versions; for hosted customers we can sign internally and provide attestations. For Private deployments you can control the signing keys and we can support HSM-based signing.
[02:19] Priya: What about data residency? Some of our data can't leave EU. Does Redwood have regional hosting?
[02:25] Dana: Yes, we have regional deployments. Hosted can be pinned to EU regions; Dedicated provides capacity in region, and Private is customer-controlled. We'll document which regions have SOC2/ISO coverage.
[02:35] Maya: There's talk of an air-gapped POC. Is that realistic?
[02:39] Samir: Yes — we have an on-prem package for air-gapped setups, but it's heavier operationally. Usually customers start with Dedicated or Private VPC and then evaluate the air-gapped package if regulatory teams require it.
[02:51] Jordan: What's the difference operationally between Dedicated and Private in your view?
[02:55] Dana: Dedicated is Redwood-managed hardware reserved for you — single-tenant pools, we still manage the control plane, but compute and data are isolated. Private hands you the control plane and optional on-prem components; you run more of the stack. Private is for the strictest compliance needs.
[03:08] Priya: For audit purposes we need full access to control-plane audit logs. Can we get those in Dedicated?
[03:13] Dana: We can provide control-plane audit logs for Dedicated under contract, with limited redaction for Redwood operational metadata. Private gives you the control plane entirely.
[03:21] Maya: Ok. Can you walk us through how request routing and fallbacks work if we want to keep latency and cost targets?
[03:28] Dana: Sure — we let you define routing policies. For example, route to lower-cost quantized variants for non-critical requests, fall back to higher-quality models if latency SLO is met. We also have automated region and capacity fallbacks. All of that is auditable and enforced via policies.
[03:41] Jordan: Are those policies stored in an auditable policy store? We need to tie changes to a user and a timestamp.
[03:48] Dana: Yes, policy changes are recorded with user, timestamp, and diffs; they can be exported.
[03:53] Priya: On the encryption front, if we use Hosted with BYOK, do you ever handle the plaintext keys?
[03:59] Samir: No — with BYOK we never see the private key material. Keys are managed in your KMS and we call through secure endpoints; we only store key references and use short-lived tokens for operations.
[04:10] Maya: How about tenant isolation? If we have multiple business units, can you enforce tenant-level separation?
[04:15] Dana: Yes. Multi-tenant isolation is enforced — data separation, separate model endpoints, and per-tenant RBAC. For the strongest guarantees we'd recommend Dedicated or Private.
[04:24] Jordan: What's your SLA for Dedicated? We have a 99.9% requirement for inference latency and throughput for critical endpoints.
[04:31] Samir: Our Dedicated SLA covers uptime and throughput tiers tied to provisioning. For latency SLOs, we guarantee tail latencies under certain traffic profiles; we'll need to run a short benchmark to validate.
[04:42] Dana: I can run a perf estimate test against your expected footprint — memory, token lengths, and concurrency — and give expected p50/p95 numbers.
[04:49] Priya: Please include cold-start and KV-cache warmup scenarios.
[04:53] Dana: Absolutely. We'll simulate prefix caching, KV cache warmup, and sudden spikes.
[04:58] Maya: On the legal/compliance side — will Redwood sign our DPA and accept encryption attestations?
[05:03] Samir: Yes. We sign standard DPAs and can work with your legal team on addenda for specific controls. We also support customer-requested data processing addenda where required.
[05:12] Jordan: How do you handle deletion requests and retention? We need the ability to purge PII from logs and model inputs within X days.
[05:18] Dana: We have purge APIs and retention policies. For Hosted we can schedule automated redaction on ingest and set TTLs for request logs. For Dedicated and Private you control policies and can enforce immediate purge using APIs.
[05:29] Priya: One concern: training data leakage. Do you ever persist customer prompts into model training corpora?
[05:35] Samir: No. By default we do not use customer data to train public models. For Hosted customers we can disable any data retention for training; for enterprise contracts we explicitly prohibit training on customer data unless agreed.
[05:47] Maya: Great. For the SOC2 artifacts, what specifically will you provide?
[05:51] Samir: We'll provide the SOC2 Type II report, the control matrix, an ISO 27001 attestation, and a summary of encryption and key management controls. We'll also include contact info for our security team for any follow-ups.
[06:02] Jordan: Ok. A couple of nitty-gritty things: 1) We require SAML assertions to include role claims; 2) we need SCIM user deprovisioning within 5 minutes.
[06:12] Dana: Both are supported. SAML role mappings can be asserted via a claim; SCIM deprovisioning latency is typically sub-minute but we'll include SLA targets.
[06:20] Priya: For audit evidence, we need logs of who changed routing policies and who re-uploaded model versions.
[06:26] Dana: That's in the audit trail — policy changes, model uploads, and deployment events are all recorded and exportable.
[06:33] Maya: We also want the ability to run a red-team style test. Can you coordinate a time window for that?
[06:38] Samir: Yes, we do scheduled security tests with customers — we can sign off on a scope and a time window. We'll bring our security engineering and coordinate.
[06:46] Jordan: On the procurement side, what are lead times for Dedicated hardware? We may need a reserve within Q1.
[06:52] Samir: Typical lead time for Dedicated pools is 6-10 weeks depending on capacity and region. Early commitment shortens lead time.
[06:59] Priya: For the air-gapped deployment, how much of the control plane needs to be local?
[07:04] Dana: The minimal air-gapped package includes model serving, the inference runtime, and local metrics collection; for full isolation you'll also host control-plane components. We have a checklist for the on-prem install.
[07:15] Maya: Can we get a high-level network diagram? We need to show it to our network team.
[07:19] Samir: Yes, we'll include a network diagram and recommended firewall rules in the pack.
[07:25] Jordan: Anything about data transformation? We sometimes tokenize and mask PII before sending. Will that affect caching or KV behavior?
[07:33] Dana: If you mask upstream, caching is applied to the masked payload, which is fine. For prefix cache effectiveness we recommend consistent masking schemes. We'll document tradeoffs.
[07:44] Maya: Regarding RBAC, we also have a requirement for separation of duties — e.g., the person who can promote a model cannot approve billing. Is Redwood flexible about custom role definitions?
[07:54] Dana: Yes, custom roles are supported. You can define granular permissions and map them to groups via SCIM or your IdP.
[08:02] Priya: How do you handle emergency access — break-glass? We need auditable break-glass workflows.
[08:08] Dana: We support temporary elevated sessions with approvals and automatic expiry, and those are fully audited.
[08:14] Jordan: For compliance reporting, do you provide a compliance-ready export pack — e.g., exported evidence bundle?
[08:21] Samir: Yes, we provide an evidence bundle for audits containing logs, config snapshots, and attestation letters.
[08:28] Maya: What about encryption key rotation? We need yearly key rotation with proof of rotation.
[08:34] Dana: Supported. We can rotate keys via your KMS and provide rotation logs for proof.
[08:41] Priya: If we want hardware-backed keys in the cloud, do you have integrations with AWS CloudHSM?
[08:46] Dana: Yes, we have integrations with AWS CloudHSM, Azure Dedicated HSM, and partner HSMs via KMIP.
[08:53] Maya: On a tangent — do you have specific guidance for embedding generation (we use embeddings for search) and responsibility for storing embedding indices?
[08:59] Dana: Embeddings can be stored in your own vector DB; Redwood can also persist embeddings in a customer-owned store. We recommend controlling embedding storage in your account for PII-sensitive vectors.
[09:11] Jordan: For the pilot, we plan to run low-risk traffic initially — 10 rps. Later we may ramp to 200 rps. Can Redwood support gradual rollouts?
[09:18] Samir: Yes — canary rollouts and A/B testing are built in. You can set traffic percentage, analyze quality regressions with our eval hooks, and automatically rollback.
[09:28] Priya: About the evals — do you keep a history of prompt sets and results for regression monitoring?
[09:33] Dana: We keep eval histories and can tie alerts to prompt sets. That can be part of Redwood Optimize.
[09:41] Maya: We need to know what personal data qualifies as sensitive under your handling. Do you provide a data classification guide?
[09:48] Samir: Yes, we'll share a data classification template and recommended redaction rules.
[09:52] Jordan: Ok, quick pricing question — difference in pricing between Hosted with BYOK and Dedicated?
[09:57] Samir: Hosted with BYOK is usage-based and simpler; Dedicated includes reserved capacity fees and a monthly commitment. We'll send a side-by-side with estimated unit economics.
[10:07] Priya: For contractual terms, do you support SOC2 attestation references in the contract?
[10:12] Samir: Yes, standard enterprise contract language references SOC2 and ISO as applicable.
[10:18] Maya: Anything else around incident response and notification SLAs?
[10:22] Dana: We have an incident response policy and standard notification windows. For enterprise customers we provide a named incident contact and faster notification targets.
[10:31] Jordan: For the POC, we'd like a short checklist of technical prerequisites — network rules, certs, and SCIM config.
[10:38] Samir: We'll send a POC readiness checklist with network ports, SAML metadata exchange steps, and sample SCIM mappings.
[10:46] Priya: For regulatory audits, we may need continuous monitoring evidence. Does Redwood have monitoring agents we can deploy?
[10:52] Dana: We provide collectors and exporters; for Private you can deploy a local exporter to your monitoring stack.
[10:58] Maya: I'm curious about the model artifact lifecycle — who can upload, sign, and deploy?
[11:03] Dana: Uploads are restricted to roles with model upload permissions. Deployments require a second approver if you enable two-person control. Artifacts are versioned and can be rolled back; deploy events are audited.
[11:14] Jordan: We need to understand how you implement data deletion guarantees across backups and caches.
[11:20] Samir: Deletion requests trigger purge of primary storage, and we have documented retention on backups. For Dedicated/Private we can coordinate a shorter backup window. We'll include an appendix on backup retention and purge processes.
[11:32] Priya: Can we get a sample list of ACLs and IAM policy templates?
[11:36] Dana: Yes, we have templates for AWS IAM, GCP IAM, and for common service accounts.
[11:41] Maya: Great. We're nearing time. Any final clarifying questions from your side?
[11:46] Jordan: One small one — do you publish third-party pen test summaries?
[11:50] Samir: Summaries are available; full reports require an NDA. We'll include the summary in the pack.
[11:57] Priya: Also please confirm support windows for Dedicated — 24/7 on-call?
[12:03] Samir: Enterprise SLAs include 24/7 on-call support for severity 1 incidents.
[12:08] Maya: Thanks. Let's recap next steps.
[12:12] Samir: Recap: 1) We'll send SOC2/ISO artifacts and our security questionnaire; 2) Dana will run perf estimates for the 10->200 rps ramp and include cache warmup; 3) We'll provide Dedicated vs Hosted pricing with BYOK comparison and a POC checklist; 4) Schedule an on-site/air-gapped feasibility call for Nov 2. Anything to add?
[12:31] Priya: Action on my side — I'll provide a short data classification excerpt and retention requirements.
[12:36] Jordan: We'll review the SOC2 docs and coordinate legal.
[12:39] Maya: Thank you.
[12:41] Samir: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up via email and log the action items.
